Package com.falkordb

Interface Reply<T extends @Nullable Object>

Type Parameters:
T - the decoded reply
All Superinterfaces:
Supplier<T>
public interface Reply<T extends @Nullable Object> extends Supplier<T>
The reply to a command queued in a GraphContext.Pipeline or a GraphContext.Transaction. It can be read once the batch has read it off the connection: after the pipeline's sync(), syncAndReturnAll() or close(), or after the transaction's exec(). A pipeline whose context was closed first can be read too, since closing the context reads what the pipeline awaited.

A graph reply is decoded the first time it is read, which can look up a label, property key or relationship type the client hasn't seen yet. Until the context is closed, read a reply on the thread that uses the context, since that lookup can run on the context's connection; after that, on one thread at a time. A reply is not safe for concurrent use.

A reply that fails to decode fails for good, even when the cause was transient. One such cause: a lookup can't run on the context's connection while another pipeline or transaction on it awaits replies, and a context the driver didn't create has no other connection to borrow, so read a reply before starting the next batch on such a context.

  • Method Details

    • get

      T get()
      Returns the decoded reply. Once the reply has been read, every call returns the same value, or throws the same exception: the server's error, or what decoding threw. An IllegalStateException for a reply that can't be read is a new one each time.
      Specified by:
      get in interface Supplier<T extends @Nullable Object>
      Returns:
      the decoded reply; null only where the server's reply to a sendCommand or sendBinaryCommand is nil, such as a GET of a missing key
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the reply can't be read: the pipeline hasn't read it yet, or its last read failed; the transaction hasn't run yet, or it was discarded, aborted because a key it watched changed, refused by the server, or exec() failed; or the context was closed before the reply was read
      GraphException - if the server answered the command with an error, or the reply can't be decoded
      RuntimeException - what else decoding the reply threw, such as the failure of a lookup it needed
